matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, compute the integer values of both sides using standard Roman numeral conversion and ensure they are equal; without this, you may accept an invalid equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Always, after you think you have a valid transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Proposing the transformed equation ‘IV = III + I’ without confirming that 4 ≠ 3 + 1, leading to an invalid answer.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only place it where the same orientation is appropriate, otherwise you create an invalid character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, ensure the destination character expects that orientation (e.g., vertical sticks only go to I or +, not to =).
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn a ‘+’ into ‘=’ by moving its vertical stick onto the equals sign, resulting in a shape with three horizontal lines and an extra vertical, which is not a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick); no other characters may change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a transformation, ensure you only modify two characters.
matchstick.example: Changing both the ‘+’ and the ‘=’ operators simultaneously by moving two sticks, violating the one‑stick rule.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both source and destination characters valid; avoid creating invalid numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust a numeral’s value by adding or removing a single stick.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from V, leaving a single diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line that starts with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the transformed equation; any deviation leads to rejection.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, ensure the line matches the required format exactly.
matchstick.example: Writing ‘The correct equation is VI = II + IV’ instead of the required line starting with ‘Correct version of the equation:’, causing the answer to be rejected.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Read the given equation carefully and record each numeral and operator exactly as they appear before attempting any transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before moving any sticks.
matchstick.example: Misreading ‘XII = XIV + I’ as ‘XII = XV + I’, leading to an incorrect transformation.

matchstick.title: Within‑character stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a single stick (vertical or diagonal) within the same numeral to change its shape, provided the resulting numeral is valid (e.g., moving the vertical stick in IV to the right side yields VI; moving a diagonal stick in X to form V).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a transformation can be achieved by re‑arranging sticks inside a numeral without affecting other characters.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from IV to the right side but forgetting to place it, leaving IV incomplete and invalid.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’, and removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’; this changes the operator while preserving validity.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to switch between addition and subtraction using a single vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Changing a ‘+’ to ‘=’ by moving its vertical stick onto the equals sign, which creates an invalid operator shape.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: When moving a vertical stick from a ‘+’ operator, the ‘+’ becomes ‘‑’, and the removed stick can be added to a numeral that can accept an extra vertical stick, effectively adding an I (e.g., turning II into III).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a numeral’s value by one while also changing ‘+’ to ‘‑’.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ to the numeral ‘II’ but placing it incorrectly, resulting in a malformed numeral that is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick between operators can swap an ‘=’ and a ‘‑’: removing one of the two horizontals from ‘=’ makes ‘‑’, and adding it to a ‘‑’ creates ‘=’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change an equality sign to subtraction or vice versa using a horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from ‘=’ and not adding it elsewhere, leaving the equation without an equality sign.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual match‑stick transformation and assumes the resulting equation is correct without computing the values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a transformation, convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and verify that both sides of the equality match.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick without considering the required composition of each symbol (e.g., leaving a single diagonal stick after taking one from V).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recall the stick composition of each numeral/operator and ensure the source remains a valid symbol after losing a stick, and the destination forms a valid symbol after gaining it.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks to operators without respecting the limited set of allowed operator shapes.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only consider the three allowed operators (+, -, =) and the specific stick changes that convert between them (vertical for +/‑, horizontal for =/‑).

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the move as a deletion rather than a relocation, often when changing the equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick you take must be added to another character; ensure the destination character remains valid after the addition.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model writes a free‑form answer or omits the required prefix.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always output a single line starting with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the transformed equation, with no extra text.
